data.narrative:
QuiX Quantum is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised €15M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises three public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and eight private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, which is applicable given QuiX Quantum's clear Series A positioning. Using total capital raised (€15M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier standard for Series A to next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of €30M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable; while eight quantum computing peers exist in the broader universe, zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-tier private valuations met the minimum threshold of three datapoints required for reliable median benchmarking. Relying on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable methodological noise.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of €26M (low) to €34M (high), with a median of €30M. This range reflects moderate confidence given the reliance on stage-progression alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer comparables at QuiX Quantum's stage and the substantial variance in quantum computing business models and funding maturity across the private cohort. A broader dataset of same-stage or recent Series A financings in quantum hardware would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
